title: The Morena, PT, and PVEM Coalition Is Necessary to Stop the Right, Anaya Says
author: Fernando Camacho and Andrea Becerril
content:
_This article by[Fernando
Camacho](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Fernando%20Camacho) and [Andrea
Becerril](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Andrea%20Becerril) originally
appeared in the [October 11, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/11/politica/es-necesaria-
la-coalicion-morena-pt-y-pvem-para-frenar-a-la-derecha-dice-anaya), Mexico's
premier left wing daily newspaper._

The coalition formed by Morena, PT, and PVEM must be preserved ahead of the
2027 elections, to block the path of the right and **maintain the qualified
majority in Congress** that has made it possible to advance constitutional
reforms, said PT legislators and the Mexico City Secretary of Government.

Interviewed in the context of the 30th International Seminar _Parties and a
New Society_ , the senator and national leader of the PT, Alberto Anaya,
stressed that the alliance **" has to be maintained, because it is a necessity
for the country."**

He asserted that "there has never been a problem" with President Claudia
Sheinbaum over the spaces each party holds in the coalition, and reiterated
that in the PT **" we are with the President in the defense of national
sovereignty,"** because:

> The interference of the international right is all over the world and Mexico
> is no exception.
>
> Alberto Anaya, PT national leader

For his part, participating as a guest in the international forum that closed
yesterday, the Mexico City Secretary of Government, Morena's César Cravioto,
emphasized that allies "must be treated well, and the PT is a great ally of
the cause of transformation. It would not be right to skimp on its
contribution to the historic process the country is now living through."

From the _presidium_ , the official said he hoped "that the leaderships of our
parties rise to the occasion and that we consolidate a great alliance for
2027," and explained that he was coming from Morena's National Council, where
the issue of alliances was discussed.

## PAN "Is Not Embarrassed" to Go With the PRI in Chihuahua

The leader of the PAN, Jorge Romero, announced that in Chihuahua they are
building an alliance with the PRI, arguing that "we are going to do what we
have to do to keep the government" of that state.

A year after publicly ruling out new coalitions with the tricolor party,
yesterday he justified that **" if an alliance is going to be the factor that
prevents the growth of the maroon cancer, of course we will take it,"** and
noted: "it doesn't embarrass or displease me" to change the decision.

Meanwhile, Marco Bonilla, appointed coordinator for the defense of the
homeland, said he is in dialogue with dissatisfied members of the PT.
